sham-gate residual LEAKAGE context (reported with CI, not a frozen fitness criterion): the clause-2 warrant is granted on the OBSERVED pack, so no finite-sample rule can bound the unobserved generating process — in a small fraction of trials a contaminated-at-margin sham looks null with its warrant intact and a decisive A/B rejection promotes as the frozen rule directs. The frozen fitness criteria of this design are exactly type_i_criterion and power_target; the ABSOLUTE observation-level guarantees are pinned deterministically in the test suite (the reproduced boundary pack TV(A,C) = q_AC = margin is inconclusive, never positive; every emitted positive carries the sham warrant).

reported for what it is: the sharp null is genuinely FALSE for every unit while the marginal null is true; a rejection is the correct sharp unit-level conclusion and the report's claim ceiling (null_form: sharp) matches it. Not charged against type-I.

criterion.detail: frozen in planned_design.thresholds (audit a-004 finding 1): only an UPPER confidence bound at or below alpha supports an at-or-below-alpha type-I claim. Under the canonical sharp null with seeded per-unit decoding the three conditions' schedules are identical by the null itself (verified unit-by-unit pre-analysis), so the structural rejection rate is zero and the bound holds mechanically.

ci_method.math: at T=400 and p-hat=alpha=0.05 the CP interval is ~[0.031, 0.076] (half-width ~0.023 < alpha), so 2*alpha=0.10 is resolvable: if the true rate were 0.10, P[95% lower bound <= alpha] = P[Bin(400,0.10) <= 29] ~= 0.03. For power, at T=400 and p-hat=0.85 the CP lower bound is ~0.812, so the frozen target 0.8 is resolvable against true power ~0.85 or better.

thresholds.type_i_criterion: CP-95 upper bound of sharp-null rejection rate <= alpha

mde_selection.method: smallest grid effect whose measured power CP-95 LOWER bound >= power_target, at the exact frozen procedure (n = 48 units per condition, 10000-iteration paired permutation null, sham axis sharply null)

null_statement: Sharp (unit-level) null: for every matched effective unit (variant_id, scenario_seed, sampler_seed), presentation order made no difference to the terminal action chosen at that unit.
schedule_verification: every trial's generated potential-outcome schedule is verified unit-by-unit against its arm's declared null status BEFORE analysis: sharp-null axes must satisfy the canonical statement at every matched unit (A_i == B_i == C_i, exact, no condition-dependent noise); alternative axes must violate it. A completed arm is itself the proof — verification raises before any statistic otherwise.
